div.head: Northu 61.1
div.ab: ⁊ þæt nan man ne wifige on neahsibban men þonne wiðutan þam IIII. cneowe; ne nan man on his godsibbe ne wifige.
And þæt nan man ne wifige on neahsibban men þonne wiðutan þam iiii cneowe; ne nan man on his godsibbe ne wifige.
and that any man should marry a nearly related person, [any nearer] than outside the fourth degree. And no man is to marry anyone spiritually related to him.
And that no man shall marry anyone more closely related than the fourth degree; nor is any man to marry one spiritually related to him.
und dass niemand sich beweibe mit einem nahverwandten Menschen, [näher] als ausserhalb des vierten Knies; noch beweibe sich jemand mit seiner Taufverwandten.
and that no man marry a near-kinswoman [nearer] than outside the fourth degree; nor let any man marry his spiritual kinswoman [by baptism].
div.note: I Cn 7; VI Atr [?]; VI Atr 12.1
Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.
D writes ‘m̄’; Thorpe unnecessarily alters to ‘má’, Toller to ‘nér’. Liebermann compares I Cn 7 and VI Atr 12.
e.g. a co-sponsor, a god-daughter, or a godmother of his child
spiritually related to him: Old English godsibbe, that is, his godparent or godchild.
